newsitem.title: INDIA: India police station attacked, 14 killed - agency.
newsitem.headline: India police station attacked, 14 killed - agency.

text.p: Thirteen policemen and a civilian were killed on Friday when suspected left-wing extremists attacked a police station in southern India, United News of India (UNI) said.
The news agency said members of the outlawed Maoist People's War Group attacked the police station in Sirpuru village in Adilabad district of Andhra Pradesh state early on Friday.
UNI said the victims were killed by a blast. It did not elaborate.
The People's War Group has often used home-made land mines to attack police and government officials.
The group operates through the vast Dandakaranya region straddling four states -- Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Orissa.
It is one of many Maoist groups considered part of the Naxalite movement, which started in India in the 1960s when the main communist party split.
Naxalites, generally well armed, also operate in West Bengal, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh states.
